answer: To resist Sybil attacks, we utilize Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent generates a hardware-bound identity via its secure enclave. Second, the agent must lock a $5,000 bond at the network wharf. Third, the protocol verifies the unique TPM signature before any data plume is accepted. This creates a verified grove of authentic agents. An attacker would face a cost of $500,000 in bonds and 14 days of hardware provisioning for 100 nodes. It is like requiring a massive, unique iron anchor for every single vessel docking to prevent phantom ships from flooding the port.
